title: III–IV. Use of the ceremonial law
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Ye first use it performs through types, figures, and shadows. In this respect that law stands as rightly called a pedagogue toward Christ (Heb. 10:1-3; Col. 2:14, 17; Gal. 3:24; Eph. 2:14-15). — III. Ye use and abrogatio belonging toward ye ceremonial law stand as toward be observed. IV. Its use was: 1. toward hold ye ancient people under hope belonging toward ye promised goods; 2. toward distinguish Israel from ye nations by a middle wall until Christ tore it down and they coalesced into one body; 3. that occupied with this laborious worship they might neither invent other cults nor take up those invented by others.
pass_b_english: III. The use and abrogation of the ceremonial law are to be observed. IV. Its use was: 1. to hold the ancient people under hope of the promised goods; 2. to distinguish Israel from the nations by a middle wall until Christ tore it down and they coalesced into one body; 3. that occupied with this laborious worship they might neither invent other cults nor take up those invented by others.
The first use it performs through types, figures, and shadows. In this respect that law is rightly called a pedagogue to Christ (Heb. 10:1-3; Col. 2:14, 17; Gal. 3:24; Eph. 2:14-15).
source_text: III. Est autem observandus legis ceremonialis usus & abrogatio. IV. Usus illius fuit 1. ut populum veterem sub spe & expectatione promissorum bonorum contineret; 2. ut populum Israeliticum a reliquis gentibus discerneret tanquam paries intergerinus, donec diruta maceria per adventum Christi cum iis in unum corpus coalescerent; 3. ut isto operoso cultu occupati neque cultus alios ipsi confingerent neque ab aliis confictos usurparent. Primum usum praestat per typos, figuras, umbras. Hoc respectu lex illa iure merito paedagogus ad Christum appellatur. Vide Heb. 10:1-3; Col. 2:14, 17; Gal. 3:24; Eph. 2:14-15.
